newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU rejected over one million tonnes wheat export.
newsitem.headline: EU rejected over one million tonnes wheat export.

text.p: The European Commission on Tuesday confirmed it had raised wheat export taxes and rejected outstanding bids for export licences, saying the decision covered over a million tonnes of wheat.

"On Friday and Monday there were bids for just over a million tonnes of soft wheat. That was really too much so the Commission decided to block the bids and raise the export taxes," a Commission spokesman in Brussels said.
Commission regulation 1574/97 published on Tuesday confirmed that all bids for export licences between August 1 and August 4 had been rejected. It did not give a reason.
Regulation 1575/97, also just published, said the new export taxes, which include three Ecus per tonne for soft wheat, would not apply to any licences requested before August 1.

The only bids confirmed so far have been for 832,500 tonnes of soft wheat sought through the EU's daily channel in France. French traders said the extra volume of some 200,000 tonnes, bringing the total above one million, may have been sought through Britain.

The official spokesman declined to say whether the Commission would again raise taxes if domestic and world prices continued to converge. But Commission sources said aggressive bidding may well trigger the same response.
"Obviously there is the possibility that if there continue to be a lot of offers, we will again raise taxes," a source said.
Traders said that while the EU move might stop immediate demand for licences, fresh gains in the dollar could help erode the gap between French and world prices and spark further bids.
Traders are said to be using the first-come-first-served system to build up long positions in licences remaining valid until December, when European prices are most competitive.

The EU regulation confirmed the following tax levels for wheat in Ecus per tonne -- soft wheat 3.0, durum 10.0, soft wheat flour and semolina 4.0, durum flour and semolina 15.0. --Tim Hepher, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
